previous_last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU corrected the VVT activation delay so that fractional millisecond settings are honored instead of being truncated by integer division. The change affects when VVT control is allowed to start after engine start; no tune migration is required.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU fixed the VVT activation delay comparison in VvtController::onFastCallback. The configured vvtActivationDelayMs is now divided by a float MS_PER_SECOND, so fractional delays are preserved instead of being truncated by integer division. Practical effect: VVT output stays inhibited until the engine has run longer than the configured delay, and the delay now matches the value entered in TunerStudio. No tune migration is needed; existing delay values remain valid. Recheck VVT arming behavior after updating if a non-whole-millisecond delay was configured.
evidence: firmware/controllers/actuators/vvt.cpp: vvtActivationDelayMs / static_cast<float>(MS_PER_SECOND) replaces integer division
unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_vvt.cpp: new VvtActivationDelayTest parameterized over 500, 1000, 1500 ms asserting PWM stays at 0 through the delay

decisions.rationale: Formatting-only change to the VVT unit test file: include ordering and comment alignment. No firmware behavior, configuration, or user-facing documentation changes.
evidence: unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_vvt.cpp: reordered using declarations and tab-aligned comments only

decisions.rationale: Integration merge of the VVT activation delay fix. Its child commits are audited separately and the merge introduces no additional user-facing change.

last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now keeps the embedded INI drive's USB block size independent of the SD driver, while SD-card USB buffers are sized from the SD driver's own block size. The existing USB Mass Storage page is updated to describe this split and to pin its source references to the new revision. No tune, calibration, or TunerStudio setting changes are required.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU separated the USB block sizing of the embedded INI drive from the SD driver. The INI drive keeps a fixed 512-byte block size whether or not SD support is compiled in, and the SD-card USB buffer is now sized from the SD driver's block size instead of a shared constant. This matters for builders of INI-only mass-storage firmware and for boards whose SD driver uses a different block size; no TunerStudio setting or tune migration is involved. The existing USB Mass Storage page is updated to describe the split and to pin its source links to this revision.
evidence: firmware/hw_layer/dma_buffers.h: MsdBlockSize replaced by IniBlockSize = 512 with a comment that the embedded INI drive uses 512-byte blocks independently of SD support
firmware/hw_layer/dma_buffers.cpp: sdBlockBuffer now declared as uint8_t sdBlockBuffer[MMCSD_BLOCK_SIZE] instead of dma_buffers::MsdBlockSize
firmware/hw_layer/mass_storage/mass_storage_init.cpp: blkbufIni uses dma_buffers::IniBlockSize and the ramdisk blockSize constant now uses dma_buffers::IniBlockSize
firmware/CHANGELOG.md: new Fixed entry 'Keep the embedded INI drive's USB block size independent of the SD driver, while sizing SD-card USB buffers from the driver's block size.'
